tweets.text:
The most interesting lesson Jensen Huang taught me

And gave PTSD to Google executives over from his leadership at $NVDA:

Was that if a critical material can be bought out for spare change eg. ~$400m (FY2028 Photonics-SOI revenue forecast for $SOI)

And trigger tens of billions in economic impact to competitors for not securing supply:

We're going to see game theory bottleneck supply procurement actually accelerate upstream through 2027, with or without him. 

I see Morgan Stanley's list highlighting CCL, ABF, PCBs, optical module components as interesting. 

However; I'd put it through my own narrower lens, especially focusing on smaller component cost chokepoints + bottlenecks that doesn't cost much to secure capacity over. 

Deleveraging/negative sentiment is indiscriminately moving the theme up and down together, so hard to argue individual fundamentals at this point. 

Reflecting on 2026, I also prob need to be more selective of companies entering 2027:

But there's going to be a lot of outsized opportunities in bottlenecks... as new architectures like NPO/CPO emerge across the ecosystem.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
摩根士丹利：AI获利了结之后，下一轮投资主线正在浮现

2027年开始，AI产业链的投资机会可能进一步向上游材料和核心零部件扩散，ABF载板、CCL覆铜板、PCB等领域有望迎来新的供需变化。

My thesis is very narrow. It's also no longer speculation when it shows up in reported earnings. 

HBM is a very large component cost in an AI server and not what I'm arguing. There's also many bottlenecks outside of memory. 

An obvious example is $AXTI InP substrates, where not securing enough capacity (where cost is in hundreds of millions) would trigger ceilings to competitor optical programs. 

And we'd likely see accelerated procurement patterns into 2027 where capacity is hard to scale.

I think equities are much more resilient than CT thinks here 

We had a historic vol panic into normalisation — it’s possible we see worse than that sure but I think it’s more probable the index just keeps marching higher (and historical episodes of similar panic -> normalisation are confluent with this view) 

We had a 10% pullback in March - everyone thought that was the beginning of the end and we ripped to new highs

We’ve had a 6-7% pullback here right into the strongest period of seasonal flows accompanied by that extreme volatility panic and again people think it’s the end of the world for equities 

Idk unless the bottom falls out of growth momentum I don’t see significant further selling of SPX and it’s much less correlated to dollar liquidity 

Probably more of the same horrible chop and slow grind higher that rewards neither side particularly cleanly

tweets.text:
This is the biggest problem we now have to deal with 

We had consecutive news failures into ltf breakdown and all of that got unwound with a reversal to new YTD highs 

If this sticks, it is very bad — if it’s a quick pop higher and a reversal again it is less of an issue 

Sticky dollar strength up at 103 will tighten financial conditions severely (and perhaps the speed of the BTC decline is pricing some of this early) 

I was wrong on thinking the post-hot inflation print breakdown on DXY marked the Q4 top — and until we are back below 101 my dollar liquidity modelling would suggest a tightening environment out to mid Q1

Breadth of DXY acceleration is particularly bad up here (6/6 on the chart = worst breadth possible for dollar liquidity) 

Obviously that’s only one factor of many but in liquidity sensitive assets it’s particularly important (does not have the same degree of correlation to equities at all) — you can see that we can cluster at severe levels of dollar liquidity right into the lows as Bitcoin prices this particularly quickly…

tweets.text:
Nowcasting is one of the biggest sins in investing and its why being an Economist or other analytical profession doesnt make a good investor

When you are forced to cross a burning bridge to escape- your goal is to make it to the other side - its not to focus on the fact the bridge is burning

The equivalent in investing is that the other side is 5-10yrs away and your burning bridge is the next 1-2 yrs

Yes - rates are going up, gold is falling, btc is falling, AI falling, RE is falling - that is the focusing on the burning bridge

If you decide that due to that instead youll just hold cash or bonds long term as its short term attractive that is like being on the burning bridge and deciding to stay still on your bit of the bridge as it seems like the slowest burning part of the bridge - completely wrong focus

When people reference their "logic" when they invest its not actually logical at all because understanding where things are today is not the core of investing - its where things will be in the future

People get stuck nowcasting because they think 3-6 months from now is the future - which it is "logically" but that is just playing out whats already happening today there is no alpha there

Remember that when you buy something you assign status value that feeling you get due to owning it is internal its not external

That also means the ability to access that feeling exists inside you separate to anything physical 

When you realise and internalise this youll place more importance on internal awakening then searching externally

The next thing, the next purchase by giving you a short hit is tricking you to think that the external is causing that but that feeling of "value" is coming from you 

You are essentially paying others to give you what you can already give yourself 

Its easy in the materialist construct to say something like "well it makes no difference to me finanically so can buy it anyway who cares" - but you are taking away from your self and the ability to find that internal revelation and no matter how wealthy- you create something you now need to give energy to

This is not about being humble - false humility is prevalent amongst the "I dont need X to prove myself"
The "i drive an old car etc and thats real wealth" crew is just the anti establishment version of the same problem

Its just about being indifferent internally to it - noone else can do that for you and only you know
